subproblem.title: For almost every level, slice masses have finite liminf on every ball
subproblem.statement: Assume (MM), the third part of the conclusion of the parent's sibling theorem dmcbr_measure_convergence_tools (verbatim; the parent discharges it with that theorem): for every P, measures μ_j (j ∈ ℕ) on ℝ^P, continuous f : ℝ^P → ℝ, G ⊆ ℝ^P, a, b ∈ ℝ, L ∈ ℝ≥0 and Z_j : ℝ → [0, ∞] with μ_j(G ∩ {a < f < b}) < ∞ for every j and Z_j(t) ≤ L·liminf_{h→0+} h⁻¹μ_j(G ∩ {t − h < f < t}) for all j and all t ∈ (a, b), there is a measurable g : ℝ → [0, ∞] with liminf_{j→∞} Z_j(t) ≤ g(t) for L¹-a.e. t ∈ (a, b) and ∫_{(a,b)} g dL¹ ≤ L·liminf_{j→∞} μ_j(G ∩ {a < f < b}). Let P ∈ ℕ, μ_i (i ∈ ℕ) measures on ℝ^P, f : ℝ^P → ℝ continuous, L ∈ ℝ≥0 and Z_i(t, k) ∈ [0, ∞] (i, k ∈ ℕ, t ∈ ℝ) such that sup_i μ_i(B_k(0)) < ∞ for every k ∈ ℕ (B_k(0) the open ball of radius k about 0) and Z_i(t, k) ≤ L·liminf_{h→0+} h⁻¹μ_i(B_k(0) ∩ {t − h < f < t}) for all i, t, k (h⁻¹ meaning ENNReal.ofReal h⁻¹). Then for L¹-a.e. t ∈ ℝ, liminf_{i→∞} Z_i(t, k) < ∞ for every k ∈ ℕ.
subproblem.lean_statement: (∀ (P : ℕ) (μs : ℕ → Measure (Euclid P)) (f : Euclid P → ℝ) (G : Set (Euclid P)) (a b : ℝ) (L : NNReal) (Z : ℕ → ℝ → ℝ≥0∞), Continuous f → (∀ j, μs j (G ∩ {x | a < f x ∧ f x < b}) < ∞) → (∀ (j : ℕ) (t : ℝ), t ∈ Ioo a b → Z j t ≤ (L : ℝ≥0∞) * liminf (fun h : ℝ => ENNReal.ofReal h⁻¹ * μs j (G ∩ {x | t - h < f x ∧ f x < t})) (𝓝[>] 0)) → ∃ g : ℝ → ℝ≥0∞, Measurable g ∧ (∀ᵐ t ∂(volume : Measure ℝ), t ∈ Ioo a b → liminf (fun j => Z j t) atTop ≤ g t) ∧ ∫⁻ t in Ioo a b, g t ≤ (L : ℝ≥0∞) * liminf (fun j => μs j (G ∩ {x | a < f x ∧ f x < b})) atTop) → ∀ (P : ℕ) (μs : ℕ → Measure (Euclid P)) (f : Euclid P → ℝ) (L : NNReal) (Z : ℕ → ℝ → ℕ → ℝ≥0∞), Continuous f → (∀ k : ℕ, ⨆ i, μs i (ball (0 : Euclid P) k) < ∞) → (∀ (i : ℕ) (t : ℝ) (k : ℕ), Z i t k ≤ (L : ℝ≥0∞) * liminf (fun h : ℝ => ENNReal.ofReal h⁻¹ * μs i (ball (0 : Euclid P) k ∩ {x | t - h < f x ∧ f x < t})) (𝓝[>] 0)) → ∀ᵐ t ∂(volume : Measure ℝ), ∀ k : ℕ, liminf (fun i => Z i t k) atTop < ∞
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: the (MM) part of step 7 of the parent proof (good parameters), with the measures μ_i + μ'_i, the balls W_k and the summed slice majorants of that step abstracted to μ_i, B_k(0) and Z_i(t, k).
1. Fix k, m ∈ ℕ and put G := B_k(0), a := −m, b := m and Λ_k := sup_i μ_i(G) < ∞. For every j, μ_j(G ∩ {a < f < b}) ≤ μ_j(G) ≤ Λ_k < ∞, and by hypothesis Z_j(t, k) ≤ L·liminf_{h→0+} h⁻¹μ_j(G ∩ {t − h < f < t}) for all t, in particular for t ∈ (a, b). So (MM), applied with these μ_j, f, G, a, b, L and with the functions t ↦ Z_j(t, k) in the role of its Z_j, gives a measurable g : ℝ → [0, ∞] with liminf_j Z_j(t, k) ≤ g(t) for a.e. t ∈ (a, b), and ∫_{(a,b)} g ≤ L·liminf_j μ_j(G ∩ {a < f < b}) ≤ L·Λ_k < ∞ (a liminf of terms that are all ≤ Λ_k is ≤ Λ_k, and L, Λ_k are finite).
2. A measurable [0, ∞]-valued function with finite integral is finite almost everywhere (Mathlib ae_lt_top); applied to L¹ restricted to the measurable set (a, b), this says: for a.e. t ∈ ℝ, t ∈ (a, b) implies g(t) < ∞. Together with step 1: for a.e. t, t ∈ (−m, m) implies liminf_i Z_i(t, k) ≤ g(t) < ∞.
3. Countably many full-measure statements hold simultaneously almost everywhere (Mathlib ae_all_iff over k and over m): for a.e. t, for all k, m ∈ ℕ, t ∈ (−m, m) implies liminf_i Z_i(t, k) < ∞.
4. Fix such a t and any k ∈ ℕ. Choose m ∈ ℕ with m > |t|; then −m < t < m, so liminf_i Z_i(t, k) < ∞ by step 3. ∎
proof_key_steps: For each k, m ∈ ℕ apply (MM) with G = B_k(0), (a, b) = (−m, m): ∫_{(−m,m)} g ≤ L·sup_i μ_i(B_k(0)) < ∞.
A finite integral forces g < ∞ a.e. on (−m, m), so liminf_i Z_i(t, k) < ∞ for a.e. t ∈ (−m, m).
Intersect over the countably many pairs (k, m) and take m > |t|.

audit.reason: The MM premise and all remaining hypotheses match the prose and frozen sibling conjunct. Uniform ball mass bounds make each measurable majorant integrable on (-m,m). Almost-everywhere finiteness, countable intersection over k and m, and choosing m greater than |t| prove exactly the conclusion. No measurability assumption on Z is silently introduced, and no further proof construction or search is deferred.

subproblem.title: Weak limits of integer multiplicity currents with locally liminf-bounded masses are integer multiplicity
subproblem.statement: Let d ∈ ℕ. Notation: for P, n ∈ ℕ, an open U ⊆ ℝ^P, T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) and W ⊆ ℝ^P, M_W(T) ∈ [0, ∞] is the local mass, the supremum of T(ω) over test forms ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ W and Euclidean covector norm |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for every x; for T ∈ 𝒟_d(U), boundaryMassOn(T, W) := M_W(∂T) if d ≥ 1 and := 0 if d = 0; for an open V ⊆ U, T|_V ∈ 𝒟_n(V) is the domain restriction (T|_V(ω) = T(ω) for ω ∈ 𝒟^n(V) ⊆ 𝒟^n(U)); T_j ⇀ T means T_j(ω) → T(ω) for every test form ω of the common domain; B_k(0) is the open ball of radius k ∈ ℕ about 0. Assume CL(d): for all P, every open U ⊆ ℝ^P, all integer multiplicity T_j ∈ 𝒟_d(U) (j ∈ ℕ) with sup_j (M_W(T_j) + boundaryMassOn(T_j, W)) < ∞ for every open W with compact closure contained in U, and T_j ⇀ T ∈ 𝒟_d(U), the current T is integer multiplicity. Assume IML(d), the degree-d case of the conclusion of the parent's sibling theorem dmcbr_isIntegerMultiplicity_of_local (which the parent discharges with that theorem): for all P, open U ⊆ ℝ^P and X ∈ 𝒟_d(U), (1) if M_W(X) < ∞ for every open W with compact closure contained in U, and every x ∈ U has some r > 0 with B_r(x) ⊆ U and X|_{B_r(x)} integer multiplicity, then X is integer multiplicity; (2) if V ⊆ U is open and X is integer multiplicity, then X|_V is integer multiplicity. Let P ∈ ℕ and Z_i, Z ∈ 𝒟_d(ℝ^P) (i ∈ ℕ) such that every Z_i is integer multiplicity, Z_i ⇀ Z, and liminf_{i→∞} (M_{B_k(0)}(Z_i) + boundaryMassOn(Z_i, B_k(0))) < ∞ for every k ∈ ℕ. Then Z is integer multiplicity.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ d : ℕ, (∀ (P : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (Ts : ℕ → GeometricCurrentOn U d) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U d), IsOpen U → (∀ j, IsIntegerMultiplicity (Ts j)) → (∀ W : Set (Euclid P), IsOpen W → CompactlyContained W U → ⨆ j, ((Ts j).massOn W + boundaryMassOn (Ts j) W) < ∞) → WeaklyConvergesOn Ts T → IsIntegerMultiplicity T) → (∀ (P : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (X : GeometricCurrentOn U d), IsOpen U → ((∀ W : Set (Euclid P), IsOpen W → CompactlyContained W U → X.massOn W < ∞) → (∀ x ∈ U, ∃ r : ℝ, 0 < r ∧ ∃ h : ball x r ⊆ U, IsIntegerMultiplicity (X.restrictDomain h)) → IsIntegerMultiplicity X) ∧ (∀ (V : Set (Euclid P)) (h : V ⊆ U), IsOpen V → IsIntegerMultiplicity X → IsIntegerMultiplicity (X.restrictDomain h))) → ∀ (P : ℕ) (Zs : ℕ → GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) d) (Z : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) d), (∀ i, IsIntegerMultiplicity (Zs i)) → WeaklyConvergesOn Zs Z → (∀ k : ℕ, liminf (fun i => (Zs i).massOn (ball (0 : Euclid P) k) + boundaryMassOn (Zs i) (ball (0 : Euclid P) k)) atTop < ∞) → IsIntegerMultiplicity Z
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: steps 9–11 of the parent proof (closure on balls by CL(d), lower semicontinuity of mass, gluing with dmcbr_isIntegerMultiplicity_of_local), stated for an arbitrary sequence Z_i in place of the slices Z_{i,t}; the bounded subsequence of step 9 is extracted here from the liminf hypothesis. Unlike the parent, CL(d) is applied directly in B_1(x) ⊆ B_k (instead of in W_k followed by a further restriction to B_1(x)), and only the inequality M_W(T|_V) ≤ M_W(T) is used. Notation: B_k := B_k(0); for an open V, ι : 𝒟^n(V) → 𝒟^n(ℝ^P) is the inclusion of test forms (the same underlying form; SimonGMT testFormOnInclusion), so T|_V(ω) = T(ιω) for T ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P).
1. Restriction does not increase mass. Let V ⊆ ℝ^P be open, T ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) and W ⊆ ℝ^P. If ω ∈ 𝒟^n(V) is admissible for M_W(T|_V) (tsupport ω ⊆ W and |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x), then ιω is admissible for M_W(T) (same form, same support, same pointwise norms) and T|_V(ω) = T(ιω) ≤ M_W(T). Taking the supremum, M_W(T|_V) ≤ M_W(T).
2. Restriction and boundary. Let V ⊆ ℝ^P be open, T ∈ 𝒟_d(ℝ^P) and W ⊆ W'. Then boundaryMassOn(T|_V, W) ≤ boundaryMassOn(T, W'). For d = 0 both sides are 0. For d = d' + 1 and η ∈ 𝒟^{d'}(V): ∂(T|_V)(η) = T|_V(dη) = T(ι(dη)) = T(d(ιη)) = ∂T(ιη) = (∂T)|_V(η), since ι(dη) and d(ιη) are the same form; so ∂(T|_V) = (∂T)|_V (currents are determined by their values), and by step 1 and monotonicity of M_W in W, M_W(∂(T|_V)) = M_W((∂T)|_V) ≤ M_W(∂T) ≤ M_{W'}(∂T).
3. Bounded subsequences. Fix k ∈ ℕ, let a_i := M_{B_k}(Z_i) + boundaryMassOn(Z_i, B_k) ∈ [0, ∞], ℓ_k := liminf_i a_i < ∞ and C_k := ℓ_k + 1. Then C_k < ∞ and ℓ_k < C_k, so a_i < C_k for infinitely many i (Mathlib frequently_lt_of_liminf_lt), hence there is a strictly increasing φ_k : ℕ → ℕ with a_{φ_k(l)} ≤ C_k for every l (Mathlib extraction_of_frequently_atTop). As φ_k(l) → ∞, Z_{φ_k(l)}(ω) → Z(ω) for every test form ω, i.e. Z_{φ_k(l)} ⇀ Z as l → ∞.
4. Every bounded S ⊆ ℝ^P lies in some B_k with k ∈ ℕ: S ⊆ B_r(0) for some real r, and B_r(0) ⊆ B_k for any integer k ≥ r.
5. Locally finite mass of Z. Let W be open with compact closure. Then W ⊆ closure W is bounded, so W ⊆ B_k for some k (step 4). By monotonicity of M, lower semicontinuity of mass under weak convergence (SimonGMT WeaklyConvergesOn.massOn_le_liminf) along φ_k (step 3), and M_{B_k}(Z_{φ_k(l)}) ≤ a_{φ_k(l)} ≤ C_k for all l: M_W(Z) ≤ M_{B_k}(Z) ≤ liminf_l M_{B_k}(Z_{φ_k(l)}) ≤ C_k < ∞.
6. Local integer multiplicity. Let x ∈ ℝ^P and V := B_1(x), an open set; V is bounded, so choose k with V ⊆ B_k (step 4). Put Y_l := Z_{φ_k(l)}|_V ∈ 𝒟_d(V) and Y := Z|_V. (i) Each Y_l is integer multiplicity by IML(d)(2) with U := ℝ^P, because Z_{φ_k(l)} is integer multiplicity. (ii) Y_l ⇀ Y in V: for ω ∈ 𝒟^d(V), Y_l(ω) = Z_{φ_k(l)}(ιω) → Z(ιω) = Y(ω) by step 3. (iii) If W is open with compact closure contained in V, then W ⊆ V ⊆ B_k, so by steps 1 and 2 and monotonicity of M, M_W(Y_l) + boundaryMassOn(Y_l, W) ≤ M_{B_k}(Z_{φ_k(l)}) + boundaryMassOn(Z_{φ_k(l)}, B_k) = a_{φ_k(l)} ≤ C_k for every l, hence sup_l (M_W(Y_l) + boundaryMassOn(Y_l, W)) ≤ C_k < ∞. By CL(d) in the open set V, applied to (Y_l) and Y, the restriction Z|_{B_1(x)} = Y is integer multiplicity.
7. Conclusion. IML(d)(1) with U := ℝ^P applies: its mass hypothesis is step 5 and its local hypothesis is step 6 with r := 1 for every x ∈ ℝ^P (B_1(x) ⊆ ℝ^P). Hence Z is integer multiplicity. ∎
proof_key_steps: Domain restriction does not increase M_W, and ∂(T|_V) = (∂T)|_V, so boundaryMassOn(T|_V, W) ≤ boundaryMassOn(T, W') for W ⊆ W'.
From liminf_i (M_{B_k}(Z_i) + boundaryMassOn(Z_i, B_k)) < ∞ extract φ_k with these sums ≤ C_k < ∞ along φ_k; Z_{φ_k(l)} ⇀ Z.
Lower semicontinuity along φ_k gives M_W(Z) ≤ C_k whenever W ⊆ B_k: Z has locally finite mass.
For x ∈ ℝ^P, CL(d) in B_1(x) ⊆ B_k, applied to the restrictions Z_{φ_k(l)}|_{B_1(x)} (integer multiplicity by IML(d)(2), masses ≤ C_k), makes Z|_{B_1(x)} integer multiplicity.
IML(d)(1) glues these local statements: Z is integer multiplicity.

audit.reason: The prose and Lean proposition include matching CL(d), IML(d), convergence, integer-multiplicity and ballwise liminf hypotheses. The proof correctly extracts bounded subsequences, transfers mass and boundary bounds through domain restriction, applies CL(d) locally, establishes locally finite limit mass, and applies IML(d). Neither the child nor parent conclusion is assumed. The argument is complete and guides formalization directly.

subproblem.title: Combined mass bound for the slice of a represented current and the slice of its boundary
subproblem.statement: Assume (SL), the frozen statement of dimred_mbl_slice_mass_bounds (verbatim the fourth hypothesis of the parent's Lean statement): for all P, k ∈ ℕ, every open U ⊆ ℝ^P, T ∈ 𝒟_{k+1}(U), measures μ, μ' on ℝ^P finite on compact subsets of U, fields ξ of (k+1)-vectors and ξ' of k-vectors, a.e. strongly measurable for μ resp. μ', such that for μ-a.e. x, |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for every covector α, and for μ'-a.e. x, |ξ'(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for every covector α (|α| the Euclidean covector norm), T(ω) = ∫ξ(ω)dμ for all ω ∈ 𝒟^{k+1}(U) and ∂T(η) = ∫ξ'(η)dμ' for all η ∈ 𝒟^k(U), and every L-Lipschitz f : ℝ^P → ℝ (L ∈ ℝ≥0), there are A_t ∈ 𝒟_{k+1}(U), B_t ∈ 𝒟_k(U) (t ∈ ℝ) with A_t(ω) = ∫_{f<t} ξ(ω)dμ, B_t(η) = ∫_{f<t} ξ'(η)dμ', ∂A_t(η) = B_t(η) whenever tsupport η ∩ {f = t} = ∅, M_W(∂A_t − B_t) ≤ L·liminf_{h→0+} h⁻¹μ(W ∩ {t − h < f < t}) for every open W and t, and ∫_{(a,b)} M_W(∂A_t − B_t) dt ≤ L·μ(W ∩ {a < f < b}) for every open W and a, b ∈ ℝ. Let P, d ∈ ℕ, X ∈ 𝒟_{d+1}(ℝ^P), μ, μ' measures on ℝ^P with μ(K) < ∞ and μ'(K) < ∞ for every compact K, ξ : ℝ^P → Λ_{d+1}(ℝ^P) and ξ' : ℝ^P → Λ_d(ℝ^P) a.e. strongly measurable for μ resp. μ' such that for μ-a.e. x, |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for every covector α, and likewise for ξ', μ', X(ω) = ∫ξ(ω)dμ for every ω ∈ 𝒟^{d+1}(ℝ^P), ∂X(η) = ∫ξ'(η)dμ' for every η ∈ 𝒟^d(ℝ^P), and f : ℝ^P → ℝ L-Lipschitz with L ∈ ℝ≥0. Then there are A_t ∈ 𝒟_{d+1}(ℝ^P) and B_t ∈ 𝒟_d(ℝ^P) (t ∈ ℝ) with A_t(ω) = ∫_{f<t} ξ(ω)dμ and B_t(η) = ∫_{f<t} ξ'(η)dμ' for all t and all test forms, such that for every open W ⊆ ℝ^P and every t ∈ ℝ, with Z_t := ∂A_t − B_t, M_W(Z_t) + boundaryMassOn(Z_t, W) ≤ L·liminf_{h→0+} h⁻¹(μ + μ')(W ∩ {t − h < f < t}). Here boundaryMassOn(Z_t, W) = 0 if d = 0 and = M_W(∂Z_t) if d ≥ 1, h⁻¹ stands for ENNReal.ofReal h⁻¹, and all quantities lie in [0, ∞].

B t).massOn W + boundaryMassOn ((A t).boundary - B t) W ≤ (L : ℝ≥0∞) * liminf (fun h : ℝ => ENNReal.ofReal h⁻¹ * (μ + μ') (W ∩ {x | t - h < f x ∧ f x < t})) (𝓝[>] 0))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 5 of the parent proof (slicing X_i and, for d ≥ 1, ∂X_i with the representation (0, 0) of ∂∂X_i = 0), the identity ∂Z_{i,t} = −∂B_{i,t} of step 9 and the summation liminf u + liminf v ≤ liminf(u + v) of step 7, for one current X. Fix an open W and t ∈ ℝ only after step 1, and write S_h := W ∩ {t − h < f < t}.
1. First slicing. Apply (SL) with U := ℝ^P, k := d, T := X, the measures μ, μ', the fields ξ, ξ', f and L (the finiteness hypotheses of (SL) hold because μ, μ' are finite on every compact set). This gives families A_t, B_t satisfying the two required value identities and, for every open W and t, (a) M_W(∂A_t − B_t) ≤ L·liminf_{h→0+} h⁻¹μ(S_h). These A, B are the families of the conclusion.
2. Mass is invariant under negation. Let n ∈ ℕ and T_1, T_2 ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) with T_1(ζ) = −T_2(ζ) for every ζ. If ω is admissible for M_W (tsupport ω ⊆ W and |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x), so is −ω, because tsupport(−ω) = tsupport ω and the Euclidean covector norm is invariant under negation (SimonGMT covectorEuclideanNorm_neg). By linearity T_1(ω) = −T_2(ω) = T_2(−ω) ≤ M_W(T_2). Taking the supremum gives M_W(T_1) ≤ M_W(T_2), and the symmetric argument (T_2(ζ) = −T_1(ζ)) gives equality.
3. Boundary part: boundaryMassOn(Z_t, W) ≤ L·liminf_{h→0+} h⁻¹μ'(S_h). If d = 0 the left side is 0 by definition. Let d = d' + 1. Then ∂X ∈ 𝒟_{d'+1}(ℝ^P) is represented by (μ', ξ'), and its boundary ∂∂X = 0 (SimonGMT GeometricCurrentOn.boundary_boundary) is represented by the zero measure and the zero d'-vector field: the zero measure is finite on compact sets, the zero field is a.e. strongly measurable and a.e. bounded for it, and ∂∂X(ζ) = 0 = ∫ 0 d0. Apply (SL) with U := ℝ^P, k := d', T := ∂X, (μ', ξ'), (0, 0), f and L: there are A'_t ∈ 𝒟_{d'+1}(ℝ^P) and B'_t ∈ 𝒟_{d'}(ℝ^P) with A'_t(η) = ∫_{f<t} ξ'(η)dμ' = B_t(η) for every η, hence A'_t = B_t (currents are determined by their values, SimonGMT GeometricCurrentOn.ext); with B'_t(ζ) = ∫_{f<t} 0 d0 = 0 for every ζ; and with M_W(∂A'_t − B'_t) ≤ L·liminf_{h→0+} h⁻¹μ'(S_h). For ζ ∈ 𝒟^{d'}(ℝ^P): ∂Z_t(ζ) = Z_t(dζ) = A_t(d dζ) − B_t(dζ) = ∂∂A_t(ζ) − ∂B_t(ζ) = −∂B_t(ζ), since ∂∂A_t = 0, whereas (∂A'_t − B'_t)(ζ) = ∂B_t(ζ) − 0 = ∂B_t(ζ). By step 2, boundaryMassOn(Z_t, W) = M_W(∂Z_t) = M_W(∂A'_t − B'_t) ≤ L·liminf_{h→0+} h⁻¹μ'(S_h).
4. Superadditivity of liminf in [0, ∞]. For u, v : ℝ → [0, ∞] and any filter F, liminf_F u + liminf_F v ≤ liminf_F (u + v). Indeed liminf_F u = sup_{s∈F} inf_{h∈s} u(h), and likewise for v and u + v. For s, s' ∈ F and every h ∈ s ∩ s' we have inf_s u + inf_{s'} v ≤ u(h) + v(h), so inf_s u + inf_{s'} v ≤ inf_{s∩s'} (u + v) ≤ liminf_F (u + v) because s ∩ s' ∈ F. Since both index families are nonempty (univ ∈ F), the sum of the two suprema is bounded by any common bound of the pairwise sums (Mathlib ENNReal.biSup_add_biSup_le'), which gives the claim.
5. Conclusion. For every h, h⁻¹(μ + μ')(S_h) = h⁻¹μ(S_h) + h⁻¹μ'(S_h) (the sum measure is evaluated termwise; multiplication distributes over addition). With u(h) := h⁻¹μ(S_h), v(h) := h⁻¹μ'(S_h) and F := 𝓝[>]0, steps 1, 3 and 4 give M_W(Z_t) + boundaryMassOn(Z_t, W) ≤ L·liminf u + L·liminf v = L·(liminf u + liminf v) ≤ L·liminf (u + v) = L·liminf_{h→0+} h⁻¹(μ + μ')(S_h). ∎
proof_key_steps: (SL) for X with (μ, ξ), (μ', ξ') gives A_t, B_t with the value identities and M_W(∂A_t − B_t) ≤ L·liminf h⁻¹μ(S_h).
M_W is unchanged when a current is negated, since admissible forms are closed under negation.

For d ≥ 1, (SL) for ∂X with (μ', ξ') and the zero representation of ∂∂X = 0 has slices A'_t = B_t, B'_t = 0, so M_W(∂B_t) ≤ L·liminf h⁻¹μ'(S_h); as ∂Z_t = −∂B_t, boundaryMassOn(Z_t, W) obeys this bound (it is 0 for d = 0).
liminf u + liminf v ≤ liminf (u + v) in [0, ∞] and h⁻¹(μ + μ')(S_h) = h⁻¹μ(S_h) + h⁻¹μ'(S_h) combine the two bounds.

audit.reason: The exact SL premise and representation hypotheses match the prose. The second slicing application correctly uses the zero representation of the double boundary when d is positive; degree zero is handled separately. Equality of currents follows from their test-form values, negation preserves mass, and the supplied supremum/infimum argument proves ENNReal liminf superadditivity, including infinite values. These steps establish the required combined bound for the same slice families without circular reliance.
